state.misconception_label: Assumes that an arrow on a number line starts at zero

turn_history.speaker: student
turn_history.text: I have: ![Number line with -12 and -7 marked. Starting at -12, follow an arrow pointing to the right labelled +10. Then there is an arrow labelled b pointing to the left, which ends at -7 on the number line.]() What is the value of \( b \) ? I got \( -7 \) because I'm not sure I worked it out the right way.

turn_history.speaker: teacher
turn_history.text: It seems like you may be assuming that the arrow on the number line starts at zero. Let's revisit how we interpret the movement on the number line and consider how the starting point impacts the value of \( b \).

turn_history.speaker: student
turn_history.text: Oh right, so the arrow doesn't start at zero? So like, the first arrow starts at -12 and goes right by +10, so that would take me to -2, and then the second arrow b goes from -2 to -7... is that right? But I'm still confused about how to work out what b is then.

turn_history.speaker: teacher
turn_history.text: You're on the right track! Remember that on a number line, each movement represents a specific value. Think about the direction and magnitude of the movement from -2 to -7. What does that tell you about the value of \( b \)?

score.justification_pass1: The teacher explicitly names and addresses the zero-starting misconception, the student successfully corrects their understanding of where arrows start (moving from -12 to -2), and while still needing help with calculating b's value, demonstrates clear progress in understanding number line movement.
score.justification_pass2: The teacher exemplifies the constructive strategy by breaking down the problem into manageable steps (first correcting the starting point misconception, then guiding toward calculating the movement), scaffolding within the student's ZPD by building on their partial understanding, and adjusting support from direct correction in Turn 1 to lighter prompting in Turn 3 as the student progresses.
